Package org.jdesktop.lg3d.displayserver.nativewindow.x11

Class X11Compositor

java.lang.Object
org.jdesktop.lg3d.displayserver.nativewindow.x11.X11Compositor
public class X11Compositor extends Object
The lg3d X11 compositor.

This class layers Composite/Damage redirection on top of the existing X11WindowManager WM claim. It does not open its own Display connection — it shares the one owned by X11WindowManager, which already holds SubstructureRedirect on the root window (a prerequisite for CompositeRedirectSubwindows).

Lifecycle

  1. X11IntegrationModule.initialize() creates X11WindowManager (claims WM, starts event thread).
  2. It then creates this class with the WM's Display and root Window.
  3. The constructor negotiates Composite, Damage, XFixes, and MIT-SHM extensions, calls RedirectSubwindows(root, Automatic), and enumerates existing top-level windows.
  4. X11WindowManager's event loop routes extension events (DamageNotify, CursorNotify) here via dispatchExtensionEvent(Event).
  5. On shutdown, shutdown() unredirects subwindows and destroys all Damage objects.

Threading

All methods are called from the X11WindowManager event thread except shutdown() which may be called from any thread. The damageMap is a ConcurrentHashMap so Stage 3's image loader can look up damage ids from the Java 3D rendering thread without synchronization.

    • markOwnWindowAsDesktop

      public void markOwnWindowAsDesktop(int windowId)
      Exempts lg3d's own top-level window (the AWT window hosting the Canvas3D) from both WM management and Composite redirection.

      Three things happen, all required:

      1. override_redirect = true so lg3d-as-WM does not try to manage (reparent/decorate) its own output window.
      2. _NET_WM_WINDOW_TYPE = _NET_WM_WINDOW_TYPE_DESKTOP so any EWMH-aware logic treats it as the background/desktop window.
      3. CompositeUnredirectWindow so the window keeps drawing directly to the screen. RedirectSubwindows redirects all root children into offscreen pixmaps; without this, lg3d's own rendering would land in a pixmap that nothing composites back and the screen would stay black.

      The native X window id of the AWT Canvas3D host is platform- and JDK-specific to obtain (it is not exposed by WinSysAWT), so the caller supplies it. See the Stage 4 window-manager wiring.

      Parameters:
      windowId - the X window id of lg3d's own top-level window

    • exemptOwnWindow

      public void exemptOwnWindow()
      Discovers and exempts lg3d's own top-level window (the AWT window that hosts the Canvas3D) via markOwnWindowAsDesktop(int). This is the Stage 4 wiring for the compositor bootstrap responsibility that keeps lg3d-as-WM from managing (and Composite from redirecting) lg3d's own output window.

      The window id is resolved in the following order:

      1. the lg3d.x11.ownwindowid system property (decimal or 0x hex), for deterministic deployments;
      2. walking the Canvas3D's AWT component hierarchy up to its top-level Window and reading the native X handle from the AWT peer reflectively. On JDK 21 this requires --add-exports java.desktop/sun.awt=ALL-UNNAMED at runtime; if it is unavailable the discovery fails quietly.

      If neither yields an id, a warning is logged: without the exemption lg3d's own rendering is redirected into an offscreen pixmap that nothing composites back, so the physical screen would appear black.
